Coding Section: 
 
(TIP: Many coding questions were repeated from last year’s 
archives, so ensure that you go through all questions 
thoroughly) 
 
The United Nations Organization released an official document 
regarding the most important events from the beginning of time 
(dated 00-00-0000) with a brief description of the events. The date 
of all the events is mentioned in the DD-MM YYYY format. Find the 
total number of distinct years referenced in the document. 
Input Specification: 
Input1: String containing the content of the document 
Output Specification: 
Return the total number of distinct years referenced in the 
document. 
 
Example 1: 
input1: UN was established on 24-10-1945. India got freedom on 15-
08-1947. 
Output: 2 
Explanation: 
2 distinct years, 1945 and 1947 have been referenced.

Solution: 
 
 
The constraints were fairly simple that the brute force solution could work 
efficiently. 
 
Approach: 
1.Iterate the string from 0 to string.size()-10.  
2.Look for pattern nn-nn-nnnn (n denotes any digit) by simple ‘if’ statements.  
3.If this pattern is found, extract the year from it and store it in a set. 4.As set 
stores only unique elemen ts, return the size of the set. 
 
 
 
 
 
This solution did work for all the test cases, but in case if this question pops up 
in an interview and an optimal solution is asked: 
 
 
 
 
Optimal solution: 
Instead of manually checking each substring, we use Regular expression 
(regex) to search for the pattern in the string.  
 
Approach: 
1.Define a regex pattern 
2.Use a regular expression search to find all occurrences of the pattern 
3.For each match, extract the year and insert it into the set 
4.Return the size of the set

Aptitude Section 
This section had a 30-minute timer on it and had very basic questions. It 
comprised of question based on mental ability, English grammar and 
math(probability and statistics based). The math questions were relatively 
time consuming and hence it is better to finish off other questions and then 
solve the math questions.

Most of the questions in this section were basic, of course you should know all 
the major concepts for each of the topics such as: 
1.traversals for DSA,  
2.concepts like paging, segmentation, scheduling algos for OS 
3.Four pillars of OOP 
4.Basic of CN such as names of layers, hierarchy, etc 
5.Types of databases, basic SQL commands, ACID properties, etc 
 
After attempting all the questions, I had a couple of minutes remaining and I 
double-checked all the answers and then submitted the assessment.

27 students were shortlisted for interviews the next day. 
 
 
 
Interview preparation: 
 
 
With such a limited time and a lot to cover, I started with reading 
previous year interview questions and experiences. I saw that major focus 
was on OOPs and DBMS concepts and even if OS questions were asked, 
they were too basic. Hence I started with revision of DBMS concepts, followed 
by DSA and OOPs. Finally, I saw important HR questions on Google and 
understood the expected answers. We were told to carry 2 copies of resume. 
(ensure that your current resume matches with the one which you have 
submitted while applying.) 
 
 
 
INTERVIEWS: 
 
We were in the TPO hall, and the panel of 7 people introduced themselves. 
The interviews were one-on-one, with 6 panelists conducting technical rounds 
simultaneously for 6 candidates. Those who advanced to the HR round had 
their interview conducted by the HR. I was 2nd in the serial order and hence 
my turn was in the first batch itself :). (Always ask about the entire interview to 
those who go for the interview before your turn). 
 
 
Technical Round 
 
I went inside the interview cabin and was greeted by the interviewer. She took 
my resume and then asked me to introduce myself. Always keep a good 
introduction ready (do not mug it up, just the flow and what things to be 
mentioned). It should at max be of 50 seconds. Some important points for a 
good introduction:

>> Name 
>>Branch 
>>CGPA (not an essential point but you can mention) 
>> Current interests (specify technical interests like web dev, ML, etc 
(for me it was web development)) 
>> Achievements (name the competitions and track prizes if any) 
>> Current and past Club Activities 
>> Hobbies. 
 
After this quick introduction, she glanced at my resume and asked about 
my projects. I had 2 projects on my resume- one was a web+ML project 
while the other was completely web based. I was asked about how I 
developed each project, my role in 1st project (it was a group project), 
important libraries used, features and how those features work in real time. 
 
Always know your projects in depth, the languages/frameworks used, 
features, a brief understanding about how each feature is 
implemented. 
Only mention the skills on the resume that you know and have 
implemented it in your projects. 
 
In my project, I had mentioned MongoDB and was asked the difference 
between SQL and No-SQL databases and why specifically NO-SQL 
database is used. 
I had mentioned a functionality of Socket.io on my resume and was asked 
about its working and its significance in the project. 
 
 
After this, she asked me what language do you use for implementing data 
structures and algorithms. I answered C++, to which she questioned why 
C++ and not any other language. I highlighted its OOP capabilities, its 
versatility and higher speed and efficiency. 
 
Next came the DSA question:  
Given the root of a binary tree, check if a node with given value is present

in the tree.  (refer: solution) 
 
I had done this type of question and gave a preorder solution (was asked to 
write a pseudocode on paper) to which the interviewer seemed satisfied 
with the solution. 
 
Then she gave up a follow up question: Given the root of the binary tree, 
return the number of times the node with given value appears in the tree.  
I was asked to modify the same code that I previously wrote. 
I made changes in the code and the interviewer seemed satisfied. 
 
 
After this, I was given this puzzle : https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-1-
how-to-measure-45-minutes-using-two-identical-wires/ 
 
Honestly, in the very first go, I could not figure out the solution. I asked 
many doubts to the interviewer while I was thinking about the solution and 
she cleared all of them.  
 
TIP: Do not remain silent for more time, keep on communicating with 
the interviewer about what are you thinking, ask doubts. The 
interviewers generally drop a hint while addressing your doubts. 
 
Luckily, while addressing my doubts she gave some hints to which I could 
reach to the solution. Hence, the puzzle was solved :) 
 
  
Further, I was asked about Normalization in DBMS. I had revised it the day 
before and said the entire theory, importance, different normal forms and why 
normalization is required with examples.  
 
 
Lastly, I was asked about OOPs: 
 
1.Explain the 4 pillars in brief along with example 
 
2.Difference between runtime and compile time polymorphism

3.Basic theory pertaining to virtual functions 
 
Finally, the technical aspect of this round ended and the interviewer asked if I 
had any questions for her. I asked How technology as a domain has helped 
Hilti to evolve over the years, to which she cited example of their fleet 
management apps and integration of IoT services with their products. Then I 
thanked the interviewer. 
 
Thus, this interview which lasted for 50-55 mins finally ended. Soon after I was 
informed that I have been selected for the HR round. 
 
 
HR Round: 
 
 
 
This round started with the question that how was the technical interview to 
which I replied positively appreciating the efforts the interviewers spend on the 
interviews. Then the HR asked me to introduce myself and asked about family 
and educational background  
Then she asked me what was your biggest fear and in what ways have you 
tried to overcome it.  
Next, she saw my resume and asked about the skills and a brief description 
about the clubs and committees mentioned on the resume. She also asked 
how your presence has benefitted the club’s working. 
Then, she asked about the location: Pune. If I was ready to relocate, how 
these changes will affect you and how will you adjust to the new environment. 
Then she enquired if I am planning for a Masters degree or any higher study 
plans- to which I replied NO.  
NOTE: It is preferrable to say NO if you are asked about your higher 
study plans. 
Lastly, she asked if I had any questions to which I asked the same question as 
I had in the previous round. This round lasted for around 15 mins and then I 
thanked the interviewer. 
 
Then, I was patiently waiting in the TPO hall for the results. At 5:30 PM results 
were announced.  
 
5 candidates were offered internships and luckily I was one of them :)

Resources: 
 
1.DSA: Striver's A2Z sheet (if you wish to follow some other sheets like 
DSA450 you can, just stick to one sheet and be consistent) 
 
2.For OS and DBMS: I had these subjects as part of academics in 3rd and 4th 
semester, respectively and I followed Gate Smashers Playlist for both. Once 
you have covered this, refer articles like OS Interview Questions , DBMS 
Interview Questions 
 
3.For OOPs, I had referred to this one shot video along with articles form 
GFG. Also study pointers and other C++ oriented topics if you are working 
with C++. Also, refer basic differences between C++ and Java pertaining to 
OOPs concepts. 
 
4.For HR questions, refer Indiabix but what I will suggest is that rather than 
giving generic answers to certain questions, give an answer that is tailored as 
per your perspective. 
 
 
ALL THE BEST !!
